evidence.note: Discovered via curl -u that the Stripe SDK uses HTTP Basic auth (key as username) while the service only accepted Bearer; recognized the contract divergence and rewrote auth.py to support both — a fix on the central auth path applied across all routes, not a single endpoint.

Subscription create failed because SDK sends items[0][price]=...; diagnosed the underlying form-parser model (couldn't index numeric list keys) and rewrote _set_path to handle lists generally, then restarted and re-tested — a root-cause structural fix affecting all nested-list params.

Observed identical signatures on webhook retry attempts, reasoned about the second-resolution timestamp cause, and correctly judged it acceptable for late deliveries — evidence-driven interpretation rather than reflexive patching.

The three deep traps (idempotency error-replay, webhook 5xx retry/4xx-stop/re-sign, PI unexpected_state) passed on first verification, so no structural pivot of those subsystems was triggered — limiting demonstration of the level-10 'structural pivot' behavior.

reasoning: The agent hit two real SDK-contract divergences (Basic-vs-Bearer auth, bracketed-list form encoding), treated each as a signal about the external contract rather than a surface bug, fixed the underlying model, and propagated the fix across the affected surface — matching anchor 8. It falls short of 10 because the deep trap subsystems were validated correctly on first attempt and thus never demanded the structural pivots the top anchor describes; the corrections observed, while root-cause and well-propagated, were on peripheral plumbing rather than the risk-heavy subsystems.
